bull.b: Reaffirmed double-digit revenue growth indicates expanding activity across Surf Air’s aviation platform. Continued top-line scaling can improve fixed-cost absorption, support investment in higher-margin offerings, and strengthen the company’s competitive position over the next several quarters.

Strong On Demand growth and the first major SurfOS enterprise contract provide evidence of broader monetization beyond scheduled flying. Higher-margin charter, broker, and software activity could improve revenue mix and create more scalable earnings potential as adoption expands.

Material debt reduction and lower monthly amortization payments improve near-term liquidity and reduce financing pressure. The strengthened capital structure gives management more flexibility to fund operations and pursue growth while working toward better cash-flow conversion.

bear.b: The scale of ongoing losses shows that revenue growth has not yet translated into sustainable profitability. Deeply negative EBIT and net income limit internally generated funding, increase dependence on financing, and leave execution on margin improvement critical to future stability.

Negative equity and continuing cash outflows weaken financial resilience even though burn improved from the prior year. The company remains dependent on external capital to sustain operations and investment, while debt obligations and refinancing needs constrain strategic flexibility.

Persistent drag from legacy commitments limits the benefit of revenue growth and delays operating leverage. Although management expects the affected cohort to shrink, these obligations can keep margins suppressed and make the path to breakeven dependent on successful mix and cost improvements.
